recipes.name: cyril-disk-probe
recipes.description: One-step recipe loaded from disk; created but never invoked.

recipes.name: autoresearch
recipes.description: Repeatedly proposes and applies one experiment at a time, runs the benchmark, and keeps changes only when they beat the current best result.

recipes.name: feature-pipeline
recipes.description: Full feature pipeline following the Roki multi-phase pattern: single-pass requirements, a design loop with a dedicated design reviewer, an implementation plan, a code loop with two-model semantic review plus aggregation, and a requirements-based validation gate. The loops and the validation gate are fail-closed: exhausting a review loop without an APPROVED verdict, or a FAIL/missing validation verdict, aborts the run instead of completing it. Does not use Kiro spec sessions — plain workflow steps. Every referenced agent is bundled (wf-design, wf-design-reviewer, wf-planner, wf-coder, semantic_reviewer, wf-review-aggregator), so this recipe is runnable in any workspace. Inputs: 'task' (the feature request) and 'workdir' (absolute path of the repo to work in; if empty the setup step falls back to the current workspace root). A leading setup step creates a fresh timestamped run folder, so artifacts are written under <workdir>/.agents/pipeline/<yyyy-mm-dd_HH-MM-SS>/ — one isolated folder per run, so no stale files from a previous run bias a reviewer or make the first draft look like a revision.

recipes.name: goal
recipes.description: Iterative agent loop working toward a user-defined goal until verified complete or iteration budget exhausted. Suits a single verifiable outcome (e.g. 'make the test suite pass') where the agent self-declares success backed by concrete evidence; there is no external progress state, so each iteration re-derives progress from the repo itself.

recipes.name: investigate
recipes.description: Single-step read-only investigation. The orchestrator supplies a self-contained brief; a planner agent investigates and writes a findings report.

recipes.name: publish-pr
recipes.description: Opens a pull request from a branch, then watches it and responds to incoming feedback until the PR reaches a terminal state.

recipes.name: ralph
recipes.description: Loops a single coding agent against a goal, working through a JSON checklist one item at a time until every item is done. Suits decomposable work driven by a JSON checklist file: progress is durable and human-inspectable mid-run. For a single non-decomposable outcome, use the goal recipe instead.

recipes.name: semantic-review-multi-model
recipes.description: Reviews a change with two independent semantic reviewers in parallel on different models (Claude Fable 5 and GPT 5.6 Sol, both at xhigh effort), each writing its own review without seeing the other's to avoid bias, then a wf-coder aggregator (Claude Fable 5, xhigh) merges the two into a single issues-only final report grouped by Severity and sorted highest-to-lowest by combined importance/confidence (each issue: User impact / Issue / Recommendation, deduped across reviewers). A leading setup step creates a fresh timestamped run folder so every run is isolated (no overwrites, and no stale files from a previous run to bias a reviewer or the aggregator); the timestamp is generated once and shared with all steps via captured output. Inputs: 'target' (what to review: a GitHub PR URL or owner/repo#N, a CRUX/Amazon code-review link or CR-id, or a local git branch name / 'uncommitted' / 'staged') and 'workdir' (absolute path of the repo/workspace to review in and the anchor for output files; if empty the setup step falls back to the current workspace root). Artifacts are written under <workdir>/.agents/reviews/semantic-review-multi-model/<yyyy-mm-dd_HH-MM-SS>/ (review-fable-5.md, review-gpt-5.6-sol.md, final-report.md). Each reviewer self-checks that it actually has the semantic_reviewer process/format loaded and pauses via send_message('warning') if not. The semantic_reviewer and wf-coder agents are bundled, so this recipe is runnable in any workspace.
